definitions.explanation: Alcoholic drinks of Western origin, such as whisky, wine, and brandy, as distinguished from sake and other traditional Japanese drinks.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{洋酒|ようしゅ}が{好|す}きだ。
その{店|みせ}は{珍|めずら}しい{洋酒|ようしゅ}をそろえている。
examples.english: That shop stocks rare Western liquors.

examples.japanese: {贈|おく}り{物|もの}として、{有名|ゆうめい}な{銘柄|めいがら}の{洋酒|ようしゅ}を{一本|いっぽん}{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: As a gift, I picked out a bottle of a famous brand of Western liquor.

notes:
A collective term for Western-style alcoholic drinks — whisky, wine, brandy, liqueurs, and so on — contrasted with {日本酒|にほんしゅ} and other traditional Japanese drinks.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洋酒|ようしゅ}を{飲|の}む: to drink Western liquor
- {洋酒|ようしゅ}{売|う}り{場|ば}: the liquor section (of a store)
- {高級|こうきゅう}{洋酒|ようしゅ}: premium imported spirits

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和酒|わしゅ}: Japanese alcoholic drinks — the contrasting category
- {地酒|じざけ}: local sake — sake brewed by a regional brewery
